    🌶️ Pepper DS ii Core: Bell - Foundations — DesignBridge¶

    AI AGENT INSTRUCTIONS — READ FIRST, APPLY TO ALL OUTPUT

    This file is the complete visual specification for "🌶️ Pepper DS ii Core: Bell - Foundations — DesignBridge". The YAML front matter above contains the normative design tokens. The sections below explain how to apply them. Apply every rule to every line of UI, HTML, CSS, JSX, or component code you generate.

    1. Colours — Use only exact hex values or var(--token) names from this file. No substitutions.
    2. Token naming — Token names in this file have no CSS prefix. In code, prepend --pepper- to every token name. Example: color-text-primary → var(--pepper-color-text-primary).
    3. Typography — Match font family, weight, size, line-height exactly.
    4. Spacing — Use only values from the spacing/sizing token tables.
    5. Border radius + shape — Use only the defined radius tokens. Apply shape rules from the Shape Rules section below: rounded for marketing/consumer/mobile contexts, square for trading/data-dense/enterprise contexts. Never mix shapes in the same UI context.
    6. Components — Mirror defined structures. Honour variant property names exactly.
    7. Shadows — Apply defined elevation styles. Do not invent shadows.
    8. Themes — Use the themes block for dark mode / multi-theme support. Apply correct mode tokens.
    9. Unknowns — If a visual decision is not defined here, ask before inventing it.

    How to Use¶

    Platform Instructions
    Claude Design Upload as design asset: Add assets → DESIGN.md, or attach in chat: "Create a design system from this DESIGN.md"
    Google Stitch Upload via Design System → DESIGN.md
    Claude Code Place in project root, reference as @DESIGN.md
    Cursor / Windsurf Add to context, prompt: "Follow @DESIGN.md for all visual decisions"
    Gemini CLI Place in project root — auto-detected by Gemini agents
    Antigravity Import via Design System settings
    GitHub Copilot Place in project root for automatic context
    OpenAI Codex Paste as system context before UI tasks
    Any LLM Paste at top of session as system context 
    You have the design system for "🌶️ Pepper DS ii Core: Bell - Foundations — DesignBridge" in DESIGN.md. Follow it precisely for ALL visual decisions. No deviations.

    Before You Implement¶

    Work through this checklist before writing any code against these tokens.

    • [ ] Confirm the DS version — check with your Pepper DS contact that this file matches the version your designer is working in (see Design System Summary below for the generation date)
    • [ ] Add the --pepper- prefix — token names in this file have no CSS prefix. In code, every token becomes var(--pepper-token-name). Example: color-text-primary → var(--pepper-color-text-primary)
    • [ ] Check disabled / opacity tokens — color-bg-overlay-state-disabled and related tokens are opacity values (0–1), not colors. Apply as opacity: not as a fill. See the ⚠️ comments in the YAML front matter.
    • [ ] Verify shape context — confirm with your designer whether the UI is rounded (marketing/mobile) or square (trading/data-dense) before implementing radius tokens. See the Shape Rules section below.
    • [ ] Do not edit this file — if you find an issue, raise it with your Pepper DS contact. Edits here will cause drift from the Figma source of truth.
    • [ ] Do not use this as a CDN source — copy the token values you need into your own repo's token system. Do not reference external Pepper DS CDN links unless specifically instructed.

    Shape Rules¶

    Shape must be consistent within a context. If buttons are rounded, all adjacent interactive elements (inputs, segmented controls, cards) follow. Never mix rounded and square in the same UI context.

    Shortcut rule: Match the button shape. If buttons are rounded, everything is rounded. If buttons are square, everything is square.

    When to use each¶

    Context Shape Radius token
    Marketing, onboarding, consumer-facing, mobile Rounded border-radius-full — 999px
    Trading dashboard, data-dense UI, toolbars, enterprise Square border-radius-sm (4px) or border-radius-md (8px)

    Per-component rules¶

    Button — corner radius per size

    Size Square Rounded
    XL border-radius-md — 8px border-radius-full — 999px
    LG border-radius-md — 8px border-radius-full — 999px
    MD border-radius-md — 8px border-radius-full — 999px
    SM border-radius-sm — 4px border-radius-full — 999px
    XS border-radius-sm — 4px border-radius-full — 999px

    Segmented control — follows button shape in the same context.

    Tag — always pill (border-radius-full — 999px). No square variant.

    Card — follows context shape. No pill variant — always border-radius-sm, border-radius-md, or square (0px).

    ⚠️ If you are unsure which shape context applies, confirm with your designer before implementing. Shape is set at the design level — your designer will specify rounded or square for each surface.

    Design Rules — Mandatory for AI Agents¶

    Category Rule
    Colours Use only tokens defined above. Always output as var(--token). Never hard-code.
    Typography Match family, weight, size, line-height exactly from the table above.
    Spacing Use only spacing token values. No arbitrary numbers.
    Radius Use only border-radius tokens. No arbitrary values.
    Shadows Use only defined elevation/effect styles.
    Components Replicate structures. Honour variant property names.
    Themes Implement all defined themes. Use CSS custom properties with mode-specific overrides.
    HTML Output semantic HTML5 with ARIA roles. All components responsive by default.
    Unknowns If a decision is not defined here: ask the user, do not invent.

    Theme Overrides¶

    /* Theme: Tablet (source: Responsive ) */
[data-theme="tablet"] {
  --canvas-viewport-width: 768px;
  --canvas-viewport-height: 1024px;
  --canvas-canvas-columns: 8px;
  --theme-spacing-layout-gutter: 20px;
  --theme-spacing-layout-margin: 40px;
  --theme-spacing-layout-pad: 40px;
  --theme-spacing-layout-gap-lg: 40px;
  --theme-spacing-content-pad-sm: 24px;
  --theme-spacing-layout-gap-md: 24px;
  --theme-spacing-content-pad-md: 32px;
  --theme-spacing-content-gap-md: 32px;
  --theme-spacing-content-pad-lg: 40px;
  --theme-spacing-content-gap-lg: 40px;
  --theme-spacing-content-gap-xs: 16px;
  --theme-spacing-layout-gutter-stack-md: 16px;
  --theme-spacing-layout-gutter-stack-lg: 24px;
  --theme-spacing-layout-gutter-stack-sm: 8px;
  --theme-spacing-content-gap-sm: 24px;
}

    /* Theme: Mobile (source: Responsive ) */
[data-theme="mobile"] {
  --canvas-viewport-width: 375px;
  --canvas-viewport-height: 812px;
  --canvas-canvas-columns: 4px;
  --theme-spacing-layout-gutter: 8px;
  --theme-spacing-layout-margin: 20px;
  --theme-spacing-layout-pad: 20px;
  --theme-spacing-layout-gap-lg: 32px;
  --theme-spacing-content-pad-sm: 16px;
  --theme-spacing-layout-gap-md: 20px;
  --theme-spacing-content-pad-md: 24px;
  --theme-spacing-content-gap-md: 24px;
  --theme-spacing-content-pad-lg: 32px;
  --theme-spacing-content-gap-lg: 32px;
  --theme-spacing-content-gap-xs: 8px;
  --theme-spacing-layout-gutter-stack-md: 16px;
  --theme-spacing-layout-gutter-stack-lg: 24px;
  --theme-spacing-layout-gutter-stack-sm: 8px;
  --theme-spacing-content-gap-sm: 16px;
}
